headline: Shift Grid Costs to Large Energy Users
short_summary: This bill mandates that large energy users, such as data centers, bear the costs of their own grid infrastructure expansions, preventing these expenses from being passed on to residential ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential consumer advocates, Governor Abigail Spanberger, Senator L. Louise Lucas, Dominion Energy (with amendments).
news_headline: Virginia Governor Signs Legislation to Address High Energy Costs
news_summary: Governor Abigail Spanberger signed legislation aimed at lowering energy costs for Virginians by ensuring data centers and other high-load energy customers pay for new energy infrastructure investments. This includes directing regulators to assign electricity costs to data centers and preventing those costs from being passed on to other customers.

headline: Mandate Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill requires water authorities to report data center water usage to the State Water Control Board, increasing transparency on the industry's environmental impact.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Senator Kannan Srinivasan, environmental groups (e.g., The Piedmont Environmental Council), water conservation advocates, local communities.
opponents: Data center industry (due to reporting burden/transparency).
news_headline: New Virginia law requires data center water usage be made public
news_summary: A new Virginia law, championed by Senator Kannan Srinivasan, mandates that local water authorities report data center water usage, which will be made publicly available on the Department of Environmental Quality's website. This aims to provide transparency regarding the significant water consumption of data centers, a growing concern for communities.

headline: Regulate Data Center Siting and Noise
short_summary: This legislation establishes new siting requirements for data centers, including mandatory sound assessments near residential areas and schools, and allows localities to assess impacts on water, agriculture, and historic sites.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Delegate Joshua Thomas, local residents, community groups, local governments.
news_headline: Virginia, home to hundreds of data centers, adds new restrictions
news_summary: Governor Abigail Spanberger signed bills, including HB 153, to regulate data centers by introducing new siting requirements and efforts to reduce noise. This legislation mandates impact assessments on agriculture, parks, and historical sites before rezoning approval, and requires sound assessments near homes and schools within 500 feet.
